- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias or add lagged correction.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply dampening factor or reduce forecast growth rate.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60–65), model often fails to correct; add downward bias or use moving average filter.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early days (e.g., first 5–7 days); apply smoothing or reduce initial slope.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.00 → 0.5 → 1.0), model often overreacts; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day moving average, model often misjudges trend; use sentiment-adjusted moving average or weighted average.
